claims.text: The complaint places the missing-person report on July 7, 2021 and describes the cabin account.
Chandler said his parents left July 2 with unidentified friends to repair a pump/fire pit.
The July 7 evening interview summary says he did not hear or see them leave and woke about 6:15 to find them gone.
Chandler attributed a July 4 message about going to White Lake that day to his mother; the later amended complaint says the parade took place July 3 at 2 p.m.
The message date and parade date differ by one day; that discrepancy tests a specific detail of the reported trip, without establishing the parents’ location or the sender’s identity.
The next scene returns to the July 8 cabin search, as identified in Grones’s testimony; this is editorial order, not evidence that the later parade-date check caused the search.

audio.text: On July seventh, twenty twenty-one, Chandler Halderson reported his parents missing. His explanation was a trip to the family's cabin. But he hadn't witnessed their departure.

audio.text: According to the criminal complaint, he said Bart and Krista had left five days earlier with friends. They were going to repair a water pump and a fire pit. He couldn't identify those friends.

picture.description: Separate Chandler and illustrative Detective Shunk layers on an explanatory board; dated July 7 evening at the family home, not the July 8 interrogation.
picture.label: ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION · JULY 7 EVENING

audio.text: That evening, detectives asked whether he'd seen or heard them leave. The complaint records his answer in a single sentence.

audio.text: He said he'd woken at around six fifteen on Friday morning and found them gone. The distinction matters: he was describing an absence, without having witnessed the trip.

audio.text: He also reported a message from his mother on Sunday, July fourth, saying they were going to White Lake for the parade that day. But the later amended complaint places that parade on Saturday, July third. One day earlier.

picture.description: Hold the July 4 message / July 3 parade comparison, then explicitly return to July 8 for the cabin scene. No suggestion that the later parade check caused the earlier search.
picture.label: REPORTED MESSAGE: JULY 4 · PARADE: JULY 3

audio.text: That mismatch did not explain where Bart and Krista were. But it gave investigators a specific detail to check. To follow the search for them, we need to go back to July eighth—and to the cabin.
